questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using a 'requirements.txt' file in Python development?
options: It records your highest game scores
It lists all third-party package dependencies so they can be easily installed on any machine
It runs loops to verify API status
questions.explanation: Correct! requirements.txt outlines all library dependencies required to run your script, ensuring workspace consistency across development devices.

questions.question: Which terminal command is used to automatically download and install all external modules listed in a project's 'requirements.txt' file?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The '-r' flag stands for 'requirement', instructing pip to read and install all packages enumerated in the specified text file.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation 'API' stand for in software and AI engineering?
questions.explanation: Perfect! API stands for Application Programming Interface, which serves as a secure bridge allowing different software applications to talk and exchange data.

questions.question: Why do we pass a secure 'API Key' when sending prediction requests to a trained machine learning model hosted online?
options: To make the images print faster
To authenticate our request and prove we have permission to use the custom trained model
Because python functions will not execute without keys
To increase the coordinate size of bounding boxes
questions.explanation: Excellent! API Keys are unique security tokens used to authenticate requests, ensuring that only authorized users can query or consume the online model.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Define a string variable named 'api_key' with the text value 'secure_key_123', and print: 'Active Key: ' concatenated with your variable.
questions.task_hint: Write: api_key = 'secure_key_123' then print('Active Key:', api_key)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Securing key constants in variables allows you to update connection credentials easily in your configuration.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write a Python statement to print the exact string: 'API Connection Successful'.
questions.explanation: Perfect! Validating network responses confirms that secure handshakes and data pipelines are fully functional.
